words.gloss: fruits of jīmūtaka (Luffa echinata, bitter luffa, Hindi devadālī/bandāl; probable)

hindi: पके हुए, पुराने अथवा सूखे जीमूतक यानी देवदाली के फलों का चूर्ण वातपित्त में।
english: The powder of the ripe, old, or dried fruits of jīmūtaka (bitter luffa), in vātapitta.
notes: No verb is given; the earlier unit's verb of application (prayuñjīta, unit 36) is understood. paryāgata taken as 'fully come (ripe)'; vātapitta read as the joint Vāta-Pitta condition. Identification (probable): jīmūtaka = Luffa echinata Roxb. (bitter luffa; Hindi devadālī, bandāl). Some lists treat other Luffa species under this name; the unit does not say which.
lines_deva: पर्यागतानां वा जीर्णानां जीमूतकफलानां शुष्काणां वा चूर्णं वातपित्ते
lines_iast: paryāgatānāṃ vā jīrṇānāṃ jīmūtakaphalānāṃ śuṣkāṇāṃ vā cūrṇaṃ vātapitte

words.gloss: of those beginning with āragvadha (āragvadha = Cassia fistula, golden shower tree; standard; the āragvadhādi group is not listed here)
of paṭolī (Trichosanthes dioica, pointed gourd, Hindi parwal; standard)

hindi: दो या तीन को कूटकर, आरग्वध यानी अमलतास आदि ताज़े द्रव्यों में से किसी एक के अथवा पटोली यानी परवल के काढ़े में भिगोकर, मथकर, पित्त और कफ से उत्पन्न ज्वर यानी बुखार में।
english: Two or three (of them), crushed, steeped in the decoction of any one of the fresh ones beginning with āragvadha (golden shower tree) or of paṭolī (pointed gourd), and churned, in fever (jvara) born of Pitta and phlegm.

text_flags.why: possible: the neuter plural of tri is trīṇi, so dvitrāṇi looks like a damaged form

notes: Doubts: (1) navānām: 'fresh' chosen as the plainest sense; 'nine' is possible. (2) āsuta (from ā-√su) glossed 'steeped'; the exact sense is unsure. (3) The thing crushed is not named (probably the jīmūtaka fruits of the previous unit). Glossary OPEN item: niryūha, kaṣāya, kvātha all rendered 'decoction' (Hindi काढ़ा) throughout this chunk. Identifications: āragvadha = Cassia fistula L. (standard; Hindi amaltās); paṭolī = Trichosanthes dioica Roxb. (standard; Hindi parwal). The members of the āragvadhādi group are not listed in this unit.
lines_deva: द्वित्राणि वा संपोथ्यारग्वधादीनां नवानामन्यतमस्य पटोल्या वा निर्यूहेणासुतानि मथित्वा पित्तश्लेष्मजे ज्वरे
lines_iast: dvitrāṇi vā saṃpothyāragvadhādīnāṃ navānāmanyatamasya paṭolyā vā niryūheṇāsutāni mathitvā pittaśleṣmaje jvare

words.gloss: jīmūtaka powder (jīmūtaka = bitter luffa, Luffa echinata; see unit 37)

hindi: जीमूतक यानी देवदाली का चूर्ण अथवा कल्क ठंडे जल के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में।
english: Jīmūtaka powder or paste with cold water, in what is born of Pitta.
notes: The noun for 'what is born of Pitta' (probably jvara, as in unit 38) is not stated.

hindi: वही गरम जल के साथ, वात और कफ से उत्पन्न में अथवा कफ से उत्पन्न में।
english: That same, with warm (water), in what is born of Vāta and Kapha, or of Kapha.
notes: 'water' is understood from the previous unit.

words.gloss: of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu (sugarcane, Saccharum officinarum; standard) and śatāvarī (Asparagus racemosus; standard); jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka are disputed (usually Malaxis acuminata and M. muscifera, rare orchids, often replaced by substitutes in practice)

hindi: जीवक, ऋषभक, इक्षु यानी गन्ना और शतावरी में से किसी एक के स्वरस के साथ, पित्त से उत्पन्न में।
english: With the expressed juice of any one of jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, ikṣu (sugarcane) and śatāvarī (wild asparagus), in what is born of Pitta.
notes: Genitive plural followed by genitive singular anyatamasya ('of any one of them'). ikṣu is kept as a name. Identifications: ikṣu = Saccharum officinarum L., sugarcane (standard); śatāvarī = Asparagus racemosus Willd. (standard); jīvaka = Malaxis acuminata D.Don and ṛṣabhaka = Malaxis muscifera (Lindl.) Kuntze (both disputed; the true drugs are rare and substitutes are used). Jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka also belong to the jīvanīya group (see unit 61).

hindi: अथवा पहले की भाँति पकाया हुआ घृत।
english: Or ghee cooked as before.
notes: 'As before' refers back to an earlier preparation; not named here.

words.gloss: ikṣvāku (bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria, bitter-fruited form, Hindi kaṛvī laukī; probable)
in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath-trouble; dyspnoea, asthma-type), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु यानी कड़वी लौकी तो विशेष रूप से कास यानी खाँसी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, ज्वर यानी बुखार, छर्दि यानी उल्टी, विष और कफ के रोगों में प्रयोग करने योग्य है।
english: Ikṣvāku (bitter bottle gourd), however, is especially to be applied in kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath-trouble; dyspnoea), jvara (fever), chardi (vomiting), viṣa (poison) and phlegm-ailments.

text_flags.why: possible: long ī here, but the same word is spelled with short i in units 45 to 55 (variant spelling or scan error)

notes: The final member -roga may govern all the preceding members (as translated) or only śleṣma. Identification (probable): ikṣvāku = the bitter-fruited bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria (Molina) Standl. (tikta-alābu); the text does not say bitter. Disease equivalents (standard): kāsa = cough; śvāsa = breathlessness/dyspnoea (includes asthma-type illness); jvara = fever; chardi = vomiting.

words.gloss: in one whose Pitta is excessive
in fever of Pitta and Kapha
in the flowers and the rest

hindi: उसके, पुष्प और फल से रहित अवस्था के, नवपल्लवों के साथ उबाला हुआ दूध, जिसमें पित्त बढ़ा हो उसमें और पित्त तथा कफ के ज्वर में; किन्तु पुष्प आदि में प्रयोग रात-जीमूत के समान हैं।
english: Milk boiled with the sprouts of that one while it is without flower and fruit, in one whose Pitta is excessive and in fever of Pitta and Kapha; but in the case of the flowers and the rest, the applications are like those of rāta-jīmūta.

text_flags.why: 'heard' makes no sense with milk; ṛ/u confusion in the scan, śṛta = boiled
rāta is not a known word here; possible damage (perhaps a lost or altered word before jīmūtavat); kept as printed

notes: Doubtful: (1) rātajīmūtavat: reading unclear, translation follows the printed letters. (2) 'that one' (tasya) is the ikṣvāku of the previous passage. (3) a-puṣpa-phala could also mean 'not yet flowered or fruited'. Parallel: the same printed spelling śrutaṃ occurs in 05.01.24 (bhallātakavidhiśrutaṃ svarasam), also a cooking context.
lines_deva: तस्यापुष्पफलस्य प्रवालैः श्रुतं क्षीरमुद्रिक्तपित्ते पित्तकफज्वरे पुष्पादिषु तु रातजीमूतवत्प्रयोगाः
lines_iast: tasyāpuṣpaphalasya pravālaiḥ śrutaṃ kṣīramudriktapitte pittakaphajvare puṣpādiṣu tu rātajīmūtavatprayogāḥ

words.gloss: expressed juice of the ikṣvāku fruit (ikṣvāku: see unit 43)
in kapha-pīnasa (Kapha-type pīnasa: chronic nasal catarrh, rhinitis; standard)
in voice-failing (svarasāda: hoarseness, loss of voice; standard)

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु के फल का स्वरस, तिगुने दूध में तैयार किया हुआ, वमन चाहने वाला रोगी पित्त में, कफ-पीनस यानी जुकाम में और स्वरसाद यानी आवाज़ बैठने में पिए।
english: Or the patient, desiring emesis, should drink the expressed juice of the ikṣvāku fruit prepared in threefold milk, in Pitta, in kapha-pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh) and in svarasāda (hoarseness, loss of voice).
notes: triguṇa-kṣīra: 'milk three times (the quantity)' is the plain sense; the exact measure is not stated. pibeta is a middle-voice optative, kept as printed.
lines_deva: इक्ष्वाकुफलस्वरसं वा त्रिगुणक्षीरसाधितमातुरः पित्ते कफपीनसे स्वरसादे वमनार्थी पिबेत
lines_iast: ikṣvākuphalasvarasaṃ vā triguṇakṣīrasādhitamāturaḥ pitte kaphapīnase svarasāde vamanārthī pibeta

words.gloss: from which the seeds are taken out

hindi: अथवा पुराने, बीज निकाले हुए फल में दूध डाले।
english: Or one should pour milk into an old fruit from which the seeds have been taken out.
lines_deva: जीर्णे वा समुद्धृतबीजे फले क्षीरं प्रक्षिपेत्
lines_iast: jīrṇe vā samuddhṛtabīje phale kṣīraṃ prakṣipet

words.gloss: in phlegm-kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breathlessness), aruci (distaste for food; anorexia) and chardi (vomiting)

hindi: उसमें बना हुआ दही कफ के कास यानी खाँसी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, अरुचि यानी खाने में अरुचि और छर्दि यानी उल्टी में।
english: The curd formed in it, in phlegm-kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breathlessness), aruci (distaste for food, anorexia) and chardi (vomiting).

text_flags.why: śvāsa + aruc requires ā (śvāsāruc-); printed u is a likely scan error

notes: śleṣmakāsa is read as 'kāsa of phlegm'; it could also be two separate members (phlegm; kāsa).

words.gloss: in viṣa (poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment; abdominal enlargement, includes ascites), galagaṇḍa (neck-swelling; goitre), granthi (knot; nodular swelling, gland), arbuda (growth; tumour) and ślīpada (filariasis, elephantiasis of the limb)

hindi: अथवा बकरी के दूध में भिगोए हुए इक्ष्वाकु के बीज, विष, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर यानी पेट के रोग, गलगण्ड यानी घेंघा, ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ, अर्बुद यानी रसौली और श्लीपद यानी हाथीपाँव में।
english: Or ikṣvāku seeds soaked in she-goat's milk, in viṣa (poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment, abdominal enlargement), galagaṇḍa (neck-swelling, goitre), granthi (knot, nodular swelling), arbuda (growth, tumour) and ślīpada (elephantiasis, filariasis).
notes: Modern equivalents (standard): gulma = abdominal lump; galagaṇḍa = goitre; granthi = nodular swelling; arbuda = tumour; ślīpada = filariasis (elephantiasis); udara here is an ailment term, not just 'belly'.

words.gloss: inner part of the ikṣvāku fruit

in kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), viṣa (poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment; includes ascites), gara (concocted poison), gaṇḍa (swelling), granthi (nodular swelling), arbuda (tumour) and ślīpada (filariasis)

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु फल का मध्य भाग, कुष्ठ यानी कोढ़ समेत त्वचा के रोग, विष, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर यानी पेट के रोग, गर यानी बनाया हुआ विष, गण्ड, ग्रन्थि यानी गाँठ, अर्बुद यानी रसौली और श्लीपद यानी हाथीपाँव में।
english: Or the inner part of the ikṣvāku fruit, in kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), viṣa, gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment), gara (concocted poison), gaṇḍa (swelling), granthi (nodular swelling), arbuda (tumour) and ślīpada (filariasis).
notes: The printed udara-gara-gaṇḍa could be a damaged 'udara-gala-gaṇḍa' (compare unit 48); kept as printed (gara and gaṇḍa as separate members), and gara is a regular term in units 60 and 65.

words.gloss: in kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), viṣa and pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-āmaya; anaemia)

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु फल मस्तु के साथ, कुष्ठ यानी कोढ़ समेत त्वचा के रोग, विष और पाण्डु रोगों यानी रक्ताल्पता में।
english: Ikṣvāku fruit with whey, in kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy), viṣa and pale-ailments (pāṇḍvāmaya, anaemia).
notes: pāṇḍu rendered 'pale' per the glossary; āmaya 'ailment'. mastu = whey (watery part of curds).

hindi: अथवा सद्रिपक, या मधु और सैंधव सहित तक्र।
english: Or sadripaka; or buttermilk with honey and saindhava.

text_flags.why: not a recognisable word (possibly sa- 'with' plus a damaged noun); kept as printed

notes: sadripaka is not understood; it may be a damaged word. The vā may join sadripaka and takra as alternatives (as translated), or sadripaka may qualify takra ('buttermilk together with sadripaka'). saindhava glossed 'salt' as it names a kind of salt.

hindi: अथवा वही मध्य भाग, एक पल गुड़ सहित, खाए।
english: Or one should eat that same inner part together with a pala of jaggery.
notes: saguḍapalam could also mean 'with jaggery (and) a pala' (a pala of what is not clear); pala is a unit of weight.

hindi: अथवा इक्ष्वाकु फल का तेल पिए।
english: Or one should drink the oil of the ikṣvāku fruit.

words.gloss: soaked in the expressed juice of that fruit
in phlegm-fever, kāsa (cough), throat-ailments and arocaka (distaste for food; anorexia)

hindi: अथवा उसी फल के स्वरस में भिगोए हुए सत्तुओं के साथ मन्थ, कफ के ज्वर, कास यानी खाँसी, कण्ठ के रोगों और अरोचक यानी खाने में अरुचि में।
english: Or a mantha (stirred drink) with saktu (parched-grain flour) soaked in the expressed juice of that same fruit, in phlegm-fever, kāsa (cough), throat-ailments and arocaka (distaste for food, anorexia).

text_flags.why: possible: printed -bhāvitaiva does not agree with saktubhiḥ; inst. pl. bhāvitaiḥ + eva (bhāvitair eva) fits, with r lost in the scan

notes: The reading bhāvitaiva is doubtful; the repair bhāvitaiḥ eva is a guess. Alternatively bhāvitā eva (fem.) with an unstated feminine noun.

words.gloss: in Vāta-Kapha, gulma (abdominal lump) and persistent fevers

hindi: इक्ष्वाकु का कल्क मांस के रस के साथ, वात-कफ, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ और लगे रहने वाले ज्वरों में।
english: Ikṣvāku paste with meat broth, in Vāta-Kapha, gulma (abdominal lump) and persistent fevers.
notes: The compound can also be read 'in persistent fevers of Vāta, Kapha and gulma'. prasakta = 'attached, persistent'.

words.gloss: with a decoction of a prastha of bilva root (bilva = Aegle marmelos, bael; standard)
tumbī seeds (tumbī = bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; probable)

hindi: अथवा एक प्रस्थ बिल्व यानी बेल की जड़ के काढ़े में तुम्बी यानी लौकी के बीज उबाले।
english: Or one should boil tumbī (bottle gourd) seeds in a decoction of a prastha of bilva (bael) root.

text_flags.why: k-v ligature lost; kvātha = decoction
kādhayet is not a word; kvāthayet 'should boil' fits the sense

notes: prastha is a measure; whether it measures the root or the decoction is not clear. Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos (L.) Correa, bael (standard; Hindi bel); tumbī = Lagenaria siceraria (probable; the same species is also given for ikṣvāku and alābu in the standard lists, but the text names them separately and does not say bitter).

words.gloss: in which the ghee is a third part
jīmūta (probably jīmūtaka, bitter luffa), mahājālinī (unidentified), vatsaka (= kuṭaja, Holarrhena pubescens; probable) and kṛtavedhana (Luffa acutangula, ridged gourd; probable) (drug names)
trikaṭuka (set of three, lit. three pungent: śuṇṭhī dry ginger, pippalī long pepper, marica black pepper; standard)

hindi: तत्पश्चात् उसमें, जिसमें घृत तीसरा भाग है, घृत के बराबर पीसे हुए तुम्बी यानी लौकी के बीज, और उनके आधे अंश वाले जीमूत, महाजालिनी, वत्सक यानी कुटज और कृतवेधन प्रत्येक, तथा काढ़े के बराबर त्रिकटु यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च डाले।
english: Then, into that, in which the ghee is a third part, one should add tumbī (bottle gourd) seeds ground equal to the ghee, and, each at half that portion, jīmūta, mahājālinī, vatsaka (kuṭaja) and kṛtavedhana, and trikaṭuka (dry ginger, long pepper and black pepper) equal to the decoction.

text_flags.why: anusvāra lost: aṃśika 'having a portion' is needed
short u for ū in jīmūta (possible)

notes: Doubtful: (1) tribhāga taken as 'a third part' (could be 'three parts'). (2) tad-ardha-aṃśika: 'half that quantity'; which members are meant to be at half the quantity is a judgement from pratyekam. (3) 'trikaṭuka equal to the decoction' is literal; the odd quantity is not corrected here. (4) the base liquid is the decoction of unit 56. Identifications (reading of this unit stays low confidence; only the surest names enriched): trikaṭuka = śuṇṭhī (Zingiber officinale), pippalī (Piper longum), marica (Piper nigrum) (standard). vatsaka = kuṭaja, Holarrhena pubescens (Buch.-Ham.) Wall. ex G.Don = H. antidysenterica (probable; indrayava is its seed). kṛtavedhana = koṣātakī, Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb. (probable; some lists give Luffa cylindrica). jīmūta presumably = jīmūtaka (see unit 37). mahājālinī: unidentified (no identification is relied on here).
lines_deva: ततस्तस्मिंस्त्रिभागघृते घृतसमानि पिष्ट्वा तुंबीबीजानि तदर्द्धाशिकानि च प्रत्येकं जीमुतमहाजालिनीवत्सककृतवेधनानि क्वाथतुल्यमेव च त्रिकटुकमावपेत्
lines_iast: tatastasmiṃstribhāgaghṛte ghṛtasamāni piṣṭvā tuṃbībījāni tadarddhāśikāni ca pratyekaṃ jīmutamahājālinīvatsakakṛtavedhanāni kvāthatulyameva ca trikaṭukamāvapet

hindi: तत्पश्चात् फिर से पकाकर लेह तैयार करे।
english: Then, having boiled it again, one should prepare a leha (licked preparation).

text_flags.why: śrutvā means 'having heard'; sense needs 'having boiled'; the exact original form (śṛtvā, śrātvā or śrapayitvā) is uncertain

notes: The corrected form and its root are uncertain; sense 'having boiled' follows unit 44 (śṛtam). Glossary OPEN item (literal verbs for lehayet etc.) not triggered in this unit.

words.gloss: in those beginning with kāśmarya (kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea, gambhārī; standard)
in the members of the great five roots

hindi: उसे चाटकर पीछे प्रमथ्या पिए, और उसी प्रकार घृत भी; कल्प काश्मर्य यानी गम्भारी आदि चार महापञ्चमूल के अंगों में अलग-अलग कहा हुआ जानना चाहिए।
english: Having licked it, one should drink a pramathyā afterwards, and likewise ghee; the procedure (kalpa) is to be understood as stated separately in each of the four members of the great five roots, beginning with kāśmarya.

text_flags.why: possible: dh for th in pramathyā; and -ddham looks like ddhṛtam (ṛt lost): 'likewise ghee'
second suggestion for the same token: ghṛtam with the ṛ lost (compare pūrvavaddhṛtaṃ, unit 42)

notes: Doubtful: pramathyā and the ghee are conjectural repairs; the ending of the sentence (the 'four members of the great five roots') is taken literally and not explained. Group (standard): mahāpañcamūla (also called bṛhat pañcamūla) = bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, kāśmarya, pāṭalā (roots of Aegle marmelos, Premna species, Oroxylum indicum, Gmelina arborea, Stereospermum suaveolens). The text does not list them here. Bilva was dealt with in unit 56, so the 'four' are presumably the other four; this is an inference, not stated in the text. kāśmarya = Gmelina arborea Roxb. (standard).
lines_deva: तमवलिह्य प्रमध्यामनुपिबेत्तद्वद्धमेव च कल्पः काश्मर्यादिषु चतुर्षु महापञ्चमूलांगेषु पृथक्पृथगुक्तो वेदितव्यः
lines_iast: tamavalihya pramadhyāmanupibettadvaddhameva ca kalpaḥ kāśmaryādiṣu caturṣu mahāpañcamūlāṃgeṣu pṛthakpṛthagukto veditavyaḥ

words.gloss: dhāmārgava (a Luffa species; disputed whether Luffa cylindrica, sponge gourd, or L. acutangula)
in gara (concocted poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment), kāsa (cough) and ailments arising from accumulation of Kapha
located in the seat of phlegm

hindi: धामार्गव विशेष रूप से गर यानी बनाया हुआ विष, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, उदर यानी पेट के रोग, कास यानी खाँसी तथा कफ के संचय से उत्पन्न रोगों में, जो स्थिर और भारी हों उनमें, कफ के आशय में स्थित रोगों में, और कण्ठ में आश्रय वाले वात-कफ में।
english: Dhāmārgava, especially in gara (concocted poison), gulma (abdominal lump), udara (belly-ailment), kāsa (cough) and the ailments arising from an accumulation of Kapha; in those that are firm and heavy, in those located in the seat of phlegm, and in Vāta-phlegm whose seat is the throat.

text_flags.why: anusvāra after dhā is probably an error (dhāmārgava in units 62 to 64)

notes: sthireṣu and guruṣu are taken to qualify the ailments (rogeṣu). The end of the unit has no verb of application. Scope of -uttha-roga: translated as applying only to kapha-saṃcaya; it could govern all preceding members (ailments arising from gara, gulma, udara, kāsa and Kapha accumulation). Identification (disputed): dhāmārgava is a Luffa species (Cucurbitaceae); lists give Luffa cylindrica (L.) M.Roem. (sponge gourd) or Luffa acutangula (L.) Roxb., and it is sometimes confused with kṛtavedhana/koṣātakī. Not resolved here; Hindi keeps the Sanskrit name.
lines_deva: धांमार्गवो विशेषेण गरगुल्मोदरकासकफसंचयोत्थरोगेषु स्थिरेषु गुरुषु च श्लेष्माशयस्थेषु वातश्लेष्मणि च कंठाश्रये
lines_iast: dhāṃmārgavo viśeṣeṇa garagulmodarakāsakaphasaṃcayottharogeṣu sthireṣu guruṣu ca śleṣmāśayastheṣu vātaśleṣmaṇi ca kaṃṭhāśraye

words.gloss: joined with powder of any one of the jīvanīya group (members in notes)

hindi: जीवनीय गण में से किसी एक के चूर्ण से युक्त, मधु और शर्करा सहित, उन्हीं के काढ़ों से लेह तैयार करके, पित्त के गौण होने पर कफ की अवस्था में विधान करे।
english: Having prepared lehas (licked preparations) joined with the powder of any one of the jīvanīya (life-promoting) group, with honey and sugar, and made with decoctions of those, one should prescribe them in the phlegm condition in which Pitta is secondary.
notes: tat-kaṣāyaiḥ: 'their decoctions' is taken as the decoctions of the drugs just named. upasarjana literally 'accompaniment, subordinate'. Group (standard, from Caraka's jīvanīya list; the Aṣṭāṅga Saṅgraha list is expected to agree but was not checked here): jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka (licorice root). Several of these (jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, kākolī) are rare or disputed drugs.

words.gloss: with a broth of tumbaru (Zanthoxylum armatum, probable) and dhānya (literally 'grain'; some lists read dhānyaka, coriander; disputed)

hindi: धामार्गव का कल्क तुम्बरु यानी तेजबल और धान्य के यूष के साथ, विषों में।
english: Dhāmārgava paste with a broth of tumbaru and dhānya, in poisons.

text_flags.why: viṣedhu is not a word; viṣeṣu 'in poisons' fits the sense (ṣu/dhu confusion)

notes: dhānya is literally 'grain' and may here be a drug name; kept as a name in the translation. Identifications (probable): tumbaru = Zanthoxylum armatum DC. (= Z. alatum; Hindi tejbal, timur). dhānya: literally 'grain'; some lists read dhānyaka, coriander (disputed). The earlier sense note (kept as a name in the translation) is not changed.

words.gloss: kāsamarda (Senna occidentalis, coffee senna; disputed, some give Senna sophera)

hindi: सुमनः, सौमनस्या, यवानी यानी अजवायन, हरिद्रा यानी हल्दी, चोरक, हैमवती, महासहा, क्षुद्रसहा, वृश्चीव, अर्बी के बीज, पुनर्नवा और कासमर्द में से किसी एक के काढ़े के साथ, अथवा एक या दो धामार्गव, मन के विकारों में।
english: With the decoction of any one of sumanas, saumanasyā, yavānī (ajwain), haridrā (turmeric), coraka, haimavatī, mahāsahā, kṣudrasahā, vṛścīva, arbī seeds, punarnavā (hogweed) and kāsamarda, or one or two of dhāmārgava, in disorders of the mind.
notes: Doubtful: the split of the long compound (especially vṛścīva-arbī-bīja: sandhi a+a, but arbī is unknown, so the member may be damaged or the division different, e.g. vṛścī + vārbī) and saumanasyā as a drug name. 'one or two' dhāmārgava: the thing counted is not stated (fruit, part?). All names kept untranslated. Alternative syntax: dhāmārgavam (one or two) may be the main item used with the decoction of any one of the listed drugs, not a separate alternative. Unit left at low confidence: only the surest names were identified (yavānī, haridrā, punarnavā standard; kāsamarda disputed). The other names (sumanas, saumanasyā, coraka, haimavatī, mahāsahā, kṣudrasahā, vṛścīva, arbī) are not identified here because the split of the compound is itself doubtful.

words.gloss: produced from milk cooked with dhāmārgava root
cooked with the six beginning with phala

hindi: धामार्गव की जड़ से पकाए हुए दूध से उत्पन्न घृत, अथवा फल आदि छह से पकाया हुआ घृत, मन के विकारों में।
english: Ghee produced from milk cooked with the root of dhāmārgava, or ghee cooked with the six beginning with phala, in disorders of the mind.
notes: 'the six beginning with phala' (phalādi-ṣaṭ) is a group not listed here; the translation stays literal.

words.gloss: kṛtavedhana (probably Luffa acutangula, ridged gourd; probable)
in gara (concocted poison), udara (belly-ailment), gulma (abdominal lump), plīha (spleen; splenic enlargement), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga; anaemia) and swelling (śvayathu; oedema)

hindi: कृतवेधन, अत्यन्त कटु, तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण, विशेष रूप से गर, उदर, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, प्लीहा यानी तिल्ली, पाण्डु रोग यानी रक्ताल्पता और श्वयथु यानी सूजन में तैयार करे।
english: One should prepare kṛtavedhana, exceedingly pungent, sharp and hot, especially for gara, udara, gulma (abdominal lump), plīha (spleen), pale-ailments (pāṇḍu-roga, anaemia) and swelling (śvayathu, oedema).
notes: kalpayet 'should prepare, arrange' (for use). kaṭu = pungent, acrid.

words.gloss: fruit of kuṭaja (Holarrhena pubescens = H. antidysenterica, Hindi kuṛā; standard; its seeds are indrayava)
in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent
in vātaśoṇita (= vātarakta; gout-type disease), visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin infection), jvara (fever), kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy) and the rest

hindi: कुटज यानी कुड़ा का फल, दूसरी ओर, सुकुमार व्यक्तियों में, जिनमें रक्त, पित्त और कफ प्रबल हों उनमें, और वातशोणित यानी वातरक्त, विसर्प यानी फैलने वाला त्वचा का संक्रमण, ज्वर यानी बुखार, कुष्ठ यानी कोढ़ समेत त्वचा के रोग आदि में प्रयोग करे।
english: One should apply kuṭaja (kurchi) fruit, on the other hand, in delicate persons, in those in whom blood, Pitta and Kapha are prominent, and in vātaśoṇita (gout), visarpa (erysipelas), jvara (fever), kuṣṭha (skin diseases, including leprosy) and the rest.
notes: ulbaṇa-rakta-pitta-kapha could also be read as 'prominent raktapitta and Kapha'; visarpa 'spreading'; vātaśoṇita 'wind-blood'. Kept literal. Identification (standard): kuṭaja = Holarrhena pubescens (Buch.-Ham.) Wall. ex G.Don (= H. antidysenterica), Hindi kuṛā/kuṛaiyā; the seeds are indrayava. Disease equivalents (standard): vātaśoṇita = vātarakta, gout-type illness; visarpa = erysipelas-type spreading skin infection; kuṣṭha = group of skin diseases including leprosy.
lines_deva: कुटजफलं पुनः सुकुमारेषूल्बणरक्तपित्तकफेषु वातशोणितविसर्पज्वरकुष्ठादिषु च प्रयोजयेत्
lines_iast: kuṭajaphalaṃ punaḥ sukumāreṣūlbaṇaraktapittakapheṣu vātaśoṇitavisarpajvarakuṣṭhādiṣu ca prayojayet

words.gloss: with milk of arka (arka = Calotropis gigantea or C. procera, milkweed; standard; 'milk' = latex)
with the decoction of any one of the madanaphala (Randia dumetorum; standard), jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, jīvantī (Leptadenia reticulata; probable) and jīvaka roots
words.gram: m. inst. sg., dvandva and tat-puruṣa

words.gloss: with water of any one of sarṣapa (mustard, Brassica species; probable), madhūka (mahua, Madhuca longifolia; standard) and salt

hindi: कुटज फल के चूर्णों को अर्क यानी आक के दूध से सात दिन तक भिगोकर, अथवा मदनफल यानी मैनफल, जीमूतक, इक्ष्वाकु, जीवन्ती और जीवक की जड़ों में से किसी एक के काढ़े से, अथवा सर्षप यानी सरसों, मधूक यानी महुआ और लवण में से किसी एक के जल से, अथवा कुटज फल का चूर्ण कृशरा के साथ, वमन के लिए तैयार करे।
english: Having soaked kuṭaja fruit powders for seven days in the milk of arka (Calotropis), or in the decoction of any one of the madanaphala (emetic nut), jīmūtaka, ikṣvāku, jīvantī and jīvaka roots, or in water of any one of sarṣapa (mustard), madhūka (mahua) and salt, or kuṭaja fruit powder with kṛśarā, one should prepare it for emesis.

text_flags.why: extra anusvāra: cūrṇāni + arka gives cūrṇānyarka
short u and extra anusvāra: mūla + anyatama gives mūlānyatama
krū for kṛ; kṛśarā is the known word

notes: Doubtful: (1) whether 'mūla' governs all the names before it (as translated) or only jīvaka. (2) sarṣapa and madhūka kept as drug names; lavaṇa 'salt'. (3) 'iti' closes the passage and is rendered 'Thus'. (4) The grammar of the 'or with' alternatives (what is prepared) is elliptical. madanaphala is a fruit name, so 'mūla' governing the whole list (roots of madanaphala, jīmūtaka, ...) is itself doubtful. Identifications (reading stays low confidence; only the surest names enriched): arka = Calotropis gigantea (L.) Dryand. / C. procera (Aiton) Dryand. (standard; Hindi āk, madār); madanaphala = Randia dumetorum (Retz.) Poir. (standard; Hindi mainphal); madhūka = Madhuca longifolia (J.Koenig) J.F.Macbr. (standard; Hindi mahuā); sarṣapa = mustard, Brassica juncea/B. campestris (probable); jīvantī = Leptadenia reticulata (Retz.) Wight & Arn. (probable); kṛśarā = a cooked dish, in the tradition of rice and pulses with sesame (probable), not changed in the translation.
lines_deva: कुटजफलचूर्णांन्यर्कक्षीरेण सप्ताहं भावयित्वा मदनफलजीमूतकेक्ष्वाकुजीवंतीजीवकमुलांन्यतमकषायेण वा सर्षपमधूकलवणान्यतमांभसा वा कुटजफलचूर्णं क्रूशरया वा वमनाय कल्पयेदिति
lines_iast: kuṭajaphalacūrṇāṃnyarkakṣīreṇa saptāhaṃ bhāvayitvā madanaphalajīmūtakekṣvākujīvaṃtījīvakamulāṃnyatamakaṣāyeṇa vā sarṣapamadhūkalavaṇānyatamāṃbhasā vā kuṭajaphalacūrṇaṃ krūśarayā vā vamanāya kalpayediti

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है।
english: And here there is this:
notes: Lead-in formula introducing the verse in units 69 and 70. GROUPING: units 68, 69 and 70 belong together (formula, then one verse of two half-verse lines). 'this' (the verse that follows) is understood.

hindi: यह वमनों का, विशेष रूप से उपयोगी वमनों का, निर्देश है।
english: This is the indication of emetics, of those especially useful.

text_flags.why: nā lost: genitive plural vamanānām is needed for the sense and the 8-syllable line

notes: GROUPING: this unit is the first half-verse of a verse completed by unit 70 (68 is its lead-in). Doubtful: the final upayoginām has no noun; taken as 'of the useful ones' (emetics).

hindi: इस बीज से बुद्धिमान अन्यों की भी कल्पना करे।
english: With this seed, the wise one should devise others also.

text_flags.why: possible: anyān + api gives anyānapi; the anusvāra is probably a scan error

notes: GROUPING: this unit is the second half-verse completing the verse begun in unit 69. 'seed' (bīja) is used figuratively: the model from which variations may be made.

hindi: इस प्रकार वमनकल्प नामक प्रथम अध्याय।
english: Thus the first chapter, named Vamanakalpa (preparations for emesis).
notes: Chapter colophon.
